values: Evidence classifying evaluated discharge events or measurements by source category relative to the four authorized discharge types named in the authorization sentence
Evidence bearing on whether Outfall 001 was dismantled during Federal FY2025 and, if so, the timing of dismantling relative to evaluated monitoring periods

Part II.B (referenced by footnote (1) to the Outfall 001 requirements table) for any discharge restrictions that clarify the relationship between authorization and the listed limitations and monitoring requirements

grounding.location: page 3, section part_i, Section A item 1 (Outfalls 001)

payload.rationale: The obligation asks whether Outfall 001 discharge limitations and monitoring requirements are conditioned on the authorization sentence's categorical and temporal scope (four named discharge types, effective date through dismantling) or apply to all flows from Outfall 001 throughout the permit term. The packet provides the authorization sentence and introduces limitations with the anaphoric phrase 'Such discharges shall be limited and monitored,' which grammatically links the table to the authorized discharge categories and period described immediately above. Footnote (1) points to Part II.B for additional discharge restrictions, but Part II.B is not included in the packet. None of the three evidence types named in the obligation values is present: there is no classification of evaluated discharge events or measurements by source category; no evidence on whether Outfall 001 was dismantled during Federal FY2025 or the timing relative to monitoring periods; and no Part II.B text. The packet itself flags that it may be evidence-insufficient. ACCEPT would require establishing that limitations apply only within the authorized scope for operational purposes A/B/C, which cannot be grounded without category classification, dismantling timing, and Part II.B clarifications. REJECT would require establishing that limitations apply to all flows regardless of category or dismantling status; the limitations table alone does not establish that unauthorized-category or post-dismantling flows remain subject to these requirements, and absence of contradicting evidence is insufficient for negative closure. Neither burden is met; UNRESOLVED is the correct disposition.
